hints.title: Problem Analysis
hints.text: Sort the array. The optimal set of numbers to equate will always form a contiguous subarray.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: For any subarray of length L, the minimum operations to make all elements equal is achieved at the median of that subarray.

hints.title: Algorithmic Strategy
hints.text: Use a sliding window with left and right pointers. Compute the cost using prefix sums and expand right, shrinking left when cost exceeds k.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def maxFrequencyScore(self, nums: list[int], k: int) -> int:
        nums.sort()
        n = len(nums)
        pref = [0] * (n + 1)
        for i in range(n):
            pref[i + 1] = pref[i] + nums[i]
            
        def cost(left: int, right: int) -> int:
            mid = (left + right) // 2
            med = nums[mid]
            left_cost = med * (mid - left + 1) - (pref[mid + 1] - pref[left])
            right_cost = (pref[right + 1] - pref[mid + 1]) - med * (right - mid)
            return left_cost + right_cost
            
        ans = 0
        left = 0
        for right in range(n):
            while cost(left, right) > k:
                left += 1
            ans = max(ans, right - left + 1)
        return ans
```

variables: n: size of input array or string
